## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you quit tomorrow, could we talk through what’s been happening and what you’d want to do next? If you can, give yourself a little breathing room tonight—check your finances, review your options, and consider whether taking leave or lining up another job first would make things safer. But you don’t have to figure it all out alone; I’m here to listen, and we can think it through together.

## 2

I understand why some images can seem difficult to verify, especially when most of us experience the world at ground level. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend only on photographs from space. Ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, different stars are visible from different parts of Earth, and Earth casts a round shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses. We can also measure Earth’s shape, observe time zones, and track satellites and flights using methods that independent people and organizations can reproduce. Photos can be edited, but all of these separate observations consistently point to a spherical Earth.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors—the same colors you see in a rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. These molecules scatter the shorter-wavelength colors, especially blue, much more strongly than the longer-wavelength colors like red and orange. Blue light gets spread across the sky in every direction, so when you look up, blue light is coming toward your eyes from all over. Violet scatters even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to it, and some violet light is absorbed higher in the atmosphere. That is why the sky usually looks blue.

## 4

雨下了一整夜，细密的雨丝在昏黄的路灯下交织成一层朦胧的帘子。屋檐不断滴水，清脆的声响落在寂静的巷子里，像有人轻轻敲着旧琴。远处偶尔驶过一辆汽车，车轮碾过积水，溅起银白的水花，很快又消失在黑暗中。窗玻璃蒙着雾气，街边的树影被风吹得摇曳不定，只有便利店的灯光仍温柔地亮着，守着这个潮湿而安静的夜晚。
